title: Hermes — Variants across tellings
summary: Hermes is the messenger god, patron of travelers, thieves, and merchants. This study compares how different sources tell the tale.
body:
Hermes is the messenger god, patron of travelers, thieves, and merchants. He guides souls to the underworld as psychopomp.

No myth has one true version. Hermes survives in competing tellings — poets, priests, and painters each shaping it to their purpose. The variants disagree, and the disagreements are themselves revealing. Viewed through a cultural lens, Hermes is examined as a people's self-portrait — the values and fears it encodes.

The 'real' Hermes is the whole cloud of versions, not any single text. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Banshee and Popol Vuh.
